data.narrative: Debugged two multi-layer bugs by tracing requests vertically through API, DB, cache, and queue boundaries rather than checking layers in isolation, then used the same discipline on the reported duplicate-analytics regression.

dimension_scores.observation: Formed the BREAK hypothesis before reading further (delete handler's cache.del() could destroy a dedup marker IF dedup lived in Redis), then falsified or confirmed it against the fork's actual design.
dimension_scores.evidence: Predicted the namespace-collision mechanism, then verified the fork has no Redis dedup (grep) and dedup is DB-side (unique event_key).

dimension_scores.observation: Mapped all three system boundaries (cache<->DB freshness, API<->queue enqueue, worker<->API shared pool) in CONTEXT and traced Bug #9/#10 through the exact handoffs.
dimension_scores.evidence: Boundary map named cache currentness, fire-and-forget queue semantics, and the shared SessionLocal pool; VERIFY chain traced worker failure to API down across 4 layers.

dimension_scores.observation: Built live probes for both bugs: delete->404 verification for Bug #9 and create/click/delete/recreate/click counting for the duplicate-analytics scenario.
dimension_scores.evidence: verify_m6.py: 302 before delete, 404 immediately after; probe_dup.py: exactly 2 events per link after delete+recreate, no doubling.

dimension_scores.observation: Locked the namespace-separation invariant with two regression tests that would catch the exact reported regression if dedup ever moves to Redis.
dimension_scores.evidence: TestAnalyticsIdempotencyAcrossDelete: replay after invalidation is a no-op; invalidation never deletes analytics rows.

dimension_scores.observation: Documented the boundary contract explicitly (NAMESPACE OWNERSHIP) so future maintainers cannot silently reintroduce the collision.
dimension_scores.evidence: cache.py docstring declares exclusive ownership of redirect:* keys and mandates a separate analytics:dedup: prefix.

dimension_scores.observation: Clear mechanism analysis but no formal writeup artifact with timeline and owner-backed remediation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Proof files capture the trace; a standalone postmortem document is still missing.

strengths: Strict vertical-trace discipline: chose B (vertical) with reasoning tied to the module premise, not default preference.
Honest falsification: when the fork already separated the namespaces, proved it live instead of forcing a phantom fix.
Documented and enforced the boundary in code so the fix is structural, not cosmetic.
growth_areas: Produce a formal postmortem artifact with timeline and owner-backed action items.
Could have added an explicit analytics:dedup namespace check even if unused today, to make the future collision fail loudly rather than silently.
data.recommendation: Write the postmortem for the M6 incidents and consider a unit test that asserts the worker never writes to the redirect: keyspace.

public_evidence.student_action: Documented exclusive ownership of the redirect: keyspace and mandated separate analytics:dedup: prefix for any future Redis dedup; kept dedup in Postgres unique(event_key).
public_evidence.technical_detail: cache.py NAMESPACE OWNERSHIP section; analytics.py insert_click idempotency via IntegrityError on unique event_key.
public_evidence.proof: grep: no redis dedup in worker path; regression tests pass; 76 tests exit 0.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows a candidate who understands that cache invalidation is a write to a shared contract and enumerates every consumer before shipping.

public_evidence.student_action: Reproduced the reported delete+recreate scenario end-to-end and proved counts stay correct.
public_evidence.technical_detail: probe_dup.py: create->2 clicks->delete->recreate->2 clicks; DB query confirmed 2 events per link.
public_evidence.proof: link 6116: 2 events, link 6117: 2 events; old deleted link analytics 404s.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates turning a reported production symptom into a deterministic, rerunnable probe.
